name: Link
description: An interactive reference to a resource that navigates the user to a target when activated.

keyboard_interactions.action: Executes the link and navigates to the target

roles.element: element containing link text or graphic
roles.description: Identifies the element as a link (not needed on native <a>)

required_attributes.description: Computed from text content, aria-labelledby, or aria-label

optional_attributes.description: Set to 0 to include in tab sequence

notes: An <a> without href is not a link: it is not focusable, has no role, and is announced as plain text. If it has no destination it should be a <button>.
The accessible name must contain the visible text (RAWeb 6.1) — voice control users say what they see.

'Click here', 'Read more', 'Learn more' fail 6.1 when the surrounding context does not disambiguate. Screen reader users often pull up a list of all links on a page, out of context: ten identical 'Read more' entries are useless.
Indicating file format and size is good practice, NOT a RAWeb criterion. Do it — but do not cite 13.3 for it (that criterion is about accessible versions of office documents).
target='_blank' should be announced, and always needs rel='noopener'. Warn the user in the link text or with visually hidden text.
Links in a block of text must not be identified by colour alone (RAWeb 3.1). Underline them, or ensure a 3:1 contrast with surrounding text PLUS a non-colour cue on hover/focus.
Do not nest interactive elements: a <button> inside an <a> is invalid and unusable by keyboard.

raweb_criteria.reason: THE criterion for this pattern. Every link must be explicit: its purpose must be understandable, from the link text alone or from its context.
Every link must have an accessible name. An icon-only or image-only link with no name is announced as just 'link'.
aria-current must be exposed on the link representing the current page.
Links must show a visible focus indicator.
A link inside body text must not be distinguished by colour alone — underline it, or guarantee a non-colour cue.
